items.title: SCM
items.description: Deep AI search for every photo and every frame of video in any folder on macOS
items.summary: SCM, short for Screen Memories, is a new MIT-licensed Electron app for macOS that indexes every photo and every video frame in watched folders on-device, so a plain-language description retrieves matching stills and video moments without a cloud call. It offers five search modes: Files, Scenes, OCR via Tesseract in 35+ languages, Dialogue via Whisper transcription, and an optional local LLMs 'Ask' chat. The default model is CLIP ViT-L/14@336 at roughly 435MB, with 480-570ms per image on CPU and SigLIP variants offered as speed/detail trade-offs. SCM targets folders, external-drive archives, screenshots, project exports, and other collections that do not fit neatly inside Photos, providing a different boundary around users’ files compared to Apple Photos.

It includes features for generating images for Xiaohongshu, video covers, and Mondo posters, among others. The project has been released with version 0.3.0 on October 4, 2026, and is written primarily in JavaScript with a small portion in Python. It is licensed under MIT and has received 93 stars on GitHub but is currently not being watched. The project can be installed as a Skill or registered as an MCP to enable various agents to generate high-quality images.

items.title: ConceptLoom
items.description: AI-powered learning workflow for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness that maps your knowledge, builds a personalized learning path, checks understanding, and saves progress across sessions.
items.summary: The sources indicate that Codex, DeepSeek Harness, and Claude Code are prominent AI coding tools in 2026, each with unique features. Codex, powered by GPT-5.6 Sol, scores higher on Terminal-Bench compared to Claude Code, making it a preferred choice for heavy shell scripting and DevOps tasks. DeepSeek Harness v0.1 is an open-source framework released by DeepSeek, aimed at developers and researchers. While the sources do not provide a definitive ranking, Codex and Claude Code are highlighted for their performance and reasoning depth, with Codex leading in benchmark scores and Claude Code noted for its reasoning on long tasks. Open-source agents like opencode are also mentioned as free, model-agnostic alternatives.

items.title: openchart
items.description: OSS Tradingview with your own AI, free and unlimited.
items.summary: TradingView offers a free tier with AI-powered charting and technical analysis, but it does not provide the Advanced Charts and Trading Platform libraries for personal use. Instead, they offer Lightweight Charts™ which are open-source under the Apache 2.0 license for personal projects. The AI Chart Copilot extension is available for free but may have usage limits to keep it sustainable. For more advanced AI trading tools, paid options like TradeAlgo are recommended for institutional-grade data.

items.title: artex-ko
items.description: ARTEX 한국어판 · AI 자율 침투 테스트 프레임워크 현지화 (upstream: Autumn-27/ARTEX, AGPL-3.0)
items.summary: ARTEX is an open-source AI-driven autonomous penetration testing framework released under the AGPL-3.0 license. It is designed for personal research and local environment technology validation, explicitly prohibiting its use for attacking external websites, services, or networks, as well as for any destructive or criminal purposes. The framework has been linked to a suspected financial sector attack infrastructure, though no official confirmation exists that it was used in the attack on Shinhan Bank. ARTEX automates the process of asset exploration, vulnerability analysis, and security tool invocation to test system vulnerabilities.

items.title: 4DCodeBench
items.description: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
items.summary: 4DCodeBench is a benchmark for 4D inverse graphics through code generation, where agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs. Agents must translate visual observations into compact representations of scene structure and dynamics, implementing abstractions such as physical simulations to reproduce complex behavior. The benchmark evaluates this capability by curating a set of real-world videos and constructing synthetic scenes spanning diverse physical phenomena, including deformation, fluid flow, and fracture. The sources indicate that strong static reconstruction capabilities do not yet translate into reliable reconstruction of complex dynamics, and the benchmark provides a testbed for tracking progress toward agents that can interpret the dynamics of the world through code.
